title: Shipping Bill Status Check: How to Track Your Export Shipment on ICEGATE
summary: Learn shipping bill meaning, check ICEGATE shipping bill status, understand LEO and EGM details, and match export records with payments and eBRCs.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


An important step for the export of physical goods across borders from India is the generation and filing of the Shipping Bill. It also serves as proof of compliance and supports refunds of eligible taxes incurred during the creation of goods, upon satisfying the applicable conditions. Cashfree supports payment collection and remittance records for both the export of physical goods and services. Let us look at this in more detail now.


### Key Takeaways


- A Shipping Bill declares goods for export. The Let Export Order, or LEO, is customs authorisation to export.
- Check shipping bill status through ICEGATE Public Enquiries using the location, Shipping Bill number and filing date.
- LEO, EGM, refund status and bank reconciliation are separate checks. A customs status alone does not confirm receipt of export proceeds.
- Your AD bank handles applicable EDPMS reconciliation. Exporters self-generate eBRCs using bank-reported IRMs under DGFT’s prescribed process.


##


What Is a Shipping Bill and How Does It Help?


A standard cargo export order of physical goods needs a Shipping Bill which has to be filed electronically on the ICEGATE portal in India, managed by Indian Customs, or through an authorised filing channel. A Shipping Bill is a mandatory document that helps authorities clear goods for export from India. Courier and postal exports have their own declaration routes and enquiry options.


Every Shipping Bill must include details such as what goods are being sent, their volume and weight, with their value clearly mentioned. After the authorities complete the applicable assessment and confirm that the cargo matches the Shipping Bill where examination is required, the Let Export Order (LEO) is issued, officially clearing it for export. The Shipping Bill also helps with compliance, supporting evidence that the incoming foreign currency is from a legitimate trade. The Shipping Bill also serves as a supporting tax record, helping with eligible GST refunds and other government export incentives.


##


What Is the ICEGATE Portal?


[ICEGATE](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/icegate-login-registration-duty-payment-portal-guide/) is the centralized portal for the CBIC (Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs) to facilitate secure, paperless and authorized transactions between the customs department and international trade stakeholders. Designed for exporters, importers, customs brokers, logistics providers etc., it acts as a single-window digital hub where users can:


- Electronically file key trade documents (such as[Bills of Entry](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/bill-of-entry-boe/) and Shipping Bills)
- Upload supporting paperwork via e-SANCHIT
- Make online customs duty payments
- Track shipment clearance statuses in real time
- Process IGST refunds and export incentives.


ICEGATE’s main purpose is to speed up cross-border trade, by providing ease of access for every user with reduced risk of manual error, supporting applicable reporting and information exchange with organizations such as RBI, DGFT, and GSTN.


##


How and When Is an ICEGATE Shipping Bill Generated?


An ICEGATE Shipping Bill is generated before the export goods leave the country, during the pre-shipment customs clearance process. Exporters can file a Shipping Bill electronically before the cargo arrives at the port, subject to the applicable advance filing timelines for air, sea and ICD shipments.


There is a four-step process from filing an ICEGATE Shipping Bill to obtaining a Let Export Order, qualifying the physical goods for export:


1. The exporter or their authorized customs broker registers on the ICEGATE Portal.
2. Shipment details (such as HSN codes, invoice values, quantity, and destination) are submitted electronically.
3. Once submitted and accepted, the system generates the Shipping Bill number, which is then verified and assessed through the customs process.
4. After the applicable inspection and clearance, customs issues a Let Export Order (LEO), authorizing goods for export.


Note: Receiving a Shipping Bill number alone does not authorise shipment.

##


What Is the Process of Closing an Export Trade Starting with the ICEGATE Shipping Bill?


India’s export process has a digital workflow from Indian Customs (ICEGATE) through the Reserve Bank of India (EDPMS) to the Directorate General of Foreign Trade ([DGFT](https://www.dgft.gov.in/CP/) ).


The sequence begins with filing of the Shipping Bill and includes generation of an Electronic Bank Realisation Certificate (eBRC), where required. Advance payments can arrive before shipment, so the steps are not always strictly sequential.


### 1. Filing the Shipping Bill on ICEGATE


Your Customs House Agent (CHA) or you submit the Shipping Bill electronically on the ICEGATE portal with your appropriate AD Code, commercial invoice and packing list.


**Assessment:** Declaration is submitted to customs to ensure the correct classification of the product[(HSN code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/hsn-sac-code-gst/) ), the correct valuation and the correct export duty or scheme.


### 2. Goods Registration and Customs Examination


**Port Arrival:** The cargo is received at the port, the airport or Inland Container Depot (ICD) and registered in the customs system.


Customs may clear the cargo without physical examination or physically inspect the goods for confirmation with the cargo invoice, based on the Risk Management System (RMS) and applicable instructions.


### 3. Let Export Order (LEO)


The Let Export Order (LEO) is issued after the documents and any required physical check have received customs clearance.


**Significance:** The LEO is the official customs authorisation for the export of goods.


### 4. Loading and Export General Manifest (EGM)


**Departure:** The carrier loads the goods and the ship/flight leaves India.


**EGM Filing:** The shipping line or airline reports the goods have left the country to customs, this is called an Export General Manifest (EGM).


EGM filing enables subsequent processing of eligible export incentives and IGST refunds, subject to the applicable requirements and system validation. Your Shipping Bill data is forwarded to RBI’s Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS).


***Also read:[International Payment Terms for Indian Exporters](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/international-payment-terms/)***


### 5. Post-Shipment Documentation and Bank Submission


For sea freight, the Bill of Lading (BL) is issued by the carrier, and for air freight, the Airway Bill (AWB) is issued.


**Bank Submission:** You will send the export documents (Shipping Bill, Invoice, BL/AWB) to your AD bank as required for collection/negotiation under a Letter of Credit (LC), or for reconciliation under another agreed payment arrangement. An LC is not compulsory for every export.


### 6. Payment Realisation and IRM Generation


The foreign buyer makes payment directly into your Indian bank account or through an eligible collection arrangement, according to the agreed payment terms. The commercial due date and regulatory realisation deadline are different.


Once you receive the foreign currency, your bank reports an Inward Remittance Message (IRM) to DGFT and uploads the relevant transaction details to RBI’s EDPMS (Export Data Processing and Monitoring System). These are distinct reporting processes. If you use Cashfree for payment collection, check whether the applicable[e-FIRA or remittance advice](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/firc/) (Foreign Inward Remittance Advice) generated by Cashfree contains your IRM number or another payment reference, and confirm the bank-reported IRM needed for eBRC generation.


### 7. Shipping Bill Knock-Off and eBRC Generation


Your AD bank reconciles the inward payment against the outstanding Shipping Bill in EDPMS. Your bank reports IRMs to the DGFT portal. Under[DGFT’s self-certification process](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/DGFT_FAQs_on_Self-Certification_of_eBRC_dated_21-04-25.pdf) , you can then log in to the DGFT website and generate, check and download your eBRC using the bank-reported IRM and relevant export details. It evidences export realisation for the applicable purpose; EDPMS closure and eBRC generation are separate processes. The realisation and repatriation of export proceeds must be completed within the stipulated RBI timeline. Under the[RBI regulations effective from 1 October 2026](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13277&Mode=0) , the standard period for ordinary goods exports is nine months from shipment; INR-invoiced or settled exports have a twelve-month period. Earlier transactions and other categories require their applicable treatment. Extensions may be permitted by the AD bank under applicable circumstances.


##


How to Track the Status of a Shipping Bill on the ICEGATE Portal


You can track your Shipping Bill status on the ICEGATE portal without logging in, using the Public Enquiries 2.0 service. ICEGATE shipping bill tracking shows customs document information; use the carrier’s tracking service for delivery progress.


### What You Need for ICEGATE Shipping Bill Tracking


- Location / Port Code: The exact customs port or Inland Container Depot (ICD) where the bill was filed (e.g., INBLR4 for Bangalore Air Cargo).
- Shipping Bill Number: The unique reference number assigned upon filing. Copy it from your filing acknowledgement.
- Shipping Bill Date: The exact filing date, entered in the format shown on the portal.


### Step-by-Step Shipping Bill Status Tracking Process


1. Go to the official ICEGATE portal and open Services → Enquiry, following the[official Public Enquiries user manual](https://www.icegate.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-02/User%20Manual-Public%20Enquiries_v1.01.pdf) .
2. Launch Public Enquiries by clicking on Public Enquiries 2.0.
3. Navigate to Document Status and choose Shipping Bill as the document type.
4. Enter Shipment Details. Select your Location (Port Code) from the dropdown first, then enter your Shipping Bill Number and Shipping Bill Date.
5. Submit. Complete any CAPTCHA verification displayed and select Search to submit the details.


For manual, courier or postal declarations, choose the corresponding enquiry type.


### What the Shipping Bill Status Details Mean


The enquiry can show several tabs. Review the relevant information rather than treating one status as proof that the entire export is complete.


**Enquiry detail** **What to check**


Shipping Bill Details Exporter, document and declared shipment information.


Current Status Current queue, LEO date and available processing details.


EGM Status/Gateway EGM Manifest details and any integration error message.


Drawback Query Details Query text, pending action and reply details, where available.


IGST Invoice Details The[GSTIN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-goods-and-service-tax-identification-number/) and invoice information available for the declaration.


No Record Available Recheck the location, number, date and enquiry type before requesting help.


If an EGM error or customs query remains unresolved, contact the carrier or customs broker responsible for that stage. If your Shipping Bill is not visible at DGFT, check the separate DGFT Shipping Bill Integration Status enquiry. A customs query should be resolved through the appropriate customs process; an unreconciled payment should be taken up with the AD bank.


##


How Does Cashfree Fit into the Trade Workflow for Export of Goods and Services?


[Cashfree is authorized by RBI for cross-border payment aggregation](https://www.cashfree.com/international-payment-gateway/) . It supports collection, settlement in the supported currency and remittance records like e-FIRA, to assist with the applicable requirements of ICEGATE, DGFT and GST. It does not replace the exporter’s customs, bank or tax obligations.


There are two export streams, the export of physical goods (where ICEGATE has a role to play in clearance) and the export of services (where payment records support a different declaration and compliance process). Let us now look at each one of them separately.


---


### 1. Exporting Physical Goods: Cashfree, ICEGATE and the AD Bank


For physical goods, Cashfree bridges the gap between your overseas buyer’s payment and your ICEGATE Shipping Bill:


- **Local Foreign Currency Collection:** International transactions can involve fees via SWIFT. With an eligible Cashfree Global Collections arrangement, you can share virtual bank details or a supported multi-currency[payment link](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/) . Compare fees and timelines for your buyer’s location.
- **Purpose Code Tagging:** RBI has a set of[purpose codes](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/purpose-code-for-international-payments/) which are useful in tagging goods-related receipts based on the payment arrangement: either P0103 (if the buyer pays an advance against an export contract for goods) or P0102 (if you already shipped the goods and have a Shipping Bill, and the receipt realises export bills sent on collection). Confirm that the code matches the actual payment arrangement.
- **Automated INR Settlement & e-FIRA:** Cashfree then converts the payment made by the buyer into INR using the applicable FX rates and provides the applicable e-FIRA (Electronic Foreign Inward Remittance Advice) or other remittance record, as proof of receipt for that product flow.
- **Closing the Loop (EDPMS & e-BRC):** You submit the applicable Cashfree e-FIRA or remittance advice along with the Shipping Bill generated on ICEGATE and other required records to your AD bank (a bank authorized by RBI to verify compliance). Your bank then reconciles or closes the applicable EDPMS entry. IGST refunds and Duty Drawback/RoDTEP incentives for the exporter have their own eligibility and processing requirements; bank closure alone does not unlock them.


---


### 2. Exporting Services: Cashfree and Applicable Export Records


Because software, consulting, and digital services do not cross physical customs borders, an ordinary goods Shipping Bill is generally not used, making your export invoice and payment records important compliance evidence. Applicable export-declaration, payment-realisation and GST requirements still need to be met:


- **Frictionless Client Checkout:** You collect payments via Cashfree’s payment solutions with the records required for the applicable service-export route.
- **Service Purpose Code Classification:** You declare and confirm the appropriate service RBI purpose code (such as P0802 for qualifying software consultancy/implementation or P1006 for business management consulting). Match the code to the actual service and applicable declaration requirements.
- **Helps with GST:** Once the payment is settled in INR, the applicable Cashfree e-FIRA (Electronic Foreign Inward Remittance Advice) provides proof of the inward remittance. Along with the export invoice and other applicable documentation, this helps exporters maintain records of foreign payment realisation for GST compliance.


---


##


3 Tips to Reconcile Shipping Bills and Export Payments


To ensure your Cashfree[settlements reconcile](https://www.cashfree.com/settlement-and-reconciliation-guide/) cleanly with ICEGATE (for physical goods) and GST (for services), align your invoicing, purpose codes, and bank accounts before collecting funds.


### 1. Keep Goods and Services Clearly Identified


Consider Separate Invoices for Separate Supplies: Since physical goods go through customs clearance and software and other consulting services generally follow a different declaration route, separate invoices for separate supplies can simplify reconciliation. Confirm whether separate e-FIRAs are available for the payment flow; neither separate invoices nor two e-FIRAs are a universal legal requirement. Use the correct RBI purpose codes for each export. This can simplify the payment collection process, minimizing avoidable delays.


### 2. Align Cashfree With Your ICEGATE AD Code Bank


The AD Code identifies the authorised dealer bank branch associated with your Shipping Bill. Confirm the correct code and bank registration requirements with your bank and customs broker. The AD bank responsible for your Shipping Bill should be aligned with the settlement of payment from Cashfree; if another bank receives the funds, coordinate the remittance records and required bank-to-bank information. This helps finance teams reconcile export proceeds against outstanding Shipping Bills in EDPMS and facilitate the generation of e-BRCs. Ask the buyer to include both the invoice number and the Shipping Bill number reference, where available, when paying into the Cashfree virtual account, so that the references can be retained for audit matching.


***Also read:[SWIFT Money Transfers, Codes, Fees and Transfer Time](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/swift-money-transfer/)***


### 3. Prevent EDPMS and Short-Realisation Mismatches


Ensure that the buyer name on the applicable Cashfree e-FIRA matches the name of the buyer on the Shipping Bill, or retain the supporting explanation for an authorised third-party receipt. Compare local virtual accounts on Cashfree with international card links, including additional charges and FX costs, so that the settlement amount can be reconciled with the value quoted in the Shipping Bill. Document fees and permitted deductions instead of assuming the net credit must equal the gross invoice. Review open EDPMS entries monthly with your AD bank and do not wait for the applicable realisation window to end.


##


Conclusion


A Shipping Bill is central to customs clearance and shipping bill status tracking for goods exports. Cashfree supports overseas payment collection and remittance records; your customs broker, carrier and AD bank handle their respective clearance, manifest and reconciliation responsibilities.


Keep the invoice, Shipping Bill, payment reference and remittance advice aligned. The applicable Cashfree e-FIRA helps the exporter provide the proof of receipt of funds to an AD bank, which then reconciles or knocks off the value of the goods against your ICEGATE Shipping Bill in EDPMS, subject to verification. The relevant bank-reported IRM supports eBRC generation through DGFT’s prescribed process.
